set.approach: From the Horseshoe Lake lot, follow the McLeod Lake trail to the lake and go by its north shore. Where the trail begins to lose height toward Mammoth Pass, bear left and follow the obvious gully on a used trail up to the far right end of the crest. There a sandy bowl lies below a buttress on its right side, the County Line Buttress, where the route starts.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from its bolted belays. Walk back down the approach trail past McLeod Lake to the Horseshoe Lake lot.

review.notes: Approach from the area page and an independent trail write-up (Horseshoe Lake, Mammoth Pass Trail, McLeod Lake, use trail to the talus band); wall placement and any anchor/descent facts from the route's own page.

set.approach: Park in the large lot at Horseshoe Lake, at the end of Highway 203, and hike the Mammoth Pass Trail as far as McLeod Lake. Work around the lake shore to its southwest side, where a well-worn path enters the trees, then follow the use trail that climbs the hillside beside a talus slide to the snowfield and talus band beneath the walls of the crest; snow can linger there into summer. The route is the arete between Hex Route and Bush Route in Sector Zero.
